Sixteen comments

This Quebecois reel has trickled into the New England contradance repetoire by way of Kerry Elkin, Becky Tracy and others. I think it was written by accordionist Phillipe Bruneau.

Re: Le 24 Juin

Patti Kusturok:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AtDsMlINess

Patti has this one on one of her albums (“Milestone”), really nice playing at that.

The composer (Phillipe), Leopold Tremblay and Gaston Nolet:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ChGwujvARyQ

In the info of the last video, they say that Phillipe dedicated the tune (name) to Quebecers and their Patron Saint. They celebrate Jean-Baptiste on June 24th.

Mario Veillette:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wGH9mn0fkKQ

Have enjoyed all of the recordings of this tune. Còig have a really nice recording on their album “Five”. George Penk, Clyde Curley, & Susan Songer play a slower tempo version (with a third part) on one of the Portland albums. Pierre Schryer & Liz Doherty both fiddle it pretty quickly on their albums “The New Canadian Waltz”, and “Last Orders”, respectively. And the Mary Cay Brass recording of Le Juin 24 is also in a fun set of tunes.

↳ Posted by NfldWhistler on January 8th, 2019.

How can versions be described as whistle friendly (X:5) or flute friendly (X:7) when they still have E flat and B flat in the minor part? Seems the only way to make this friendly for the wind player is to switch instruments between the minor and major parts.

Re: Le 24 Juin

Well, if you read the comment I made with the posting of X5, I called it “friendlier”, which isn’t the same as “friendly”.

And yes, one part would be easier than the other on different whistles (e.g., A Part for C Whistle, B Part for D Whistle), though switching whistles between parts isn’t exactly practical for continuous playing. ​

Le 24 Juin, X:8

A handful of modifications to X5, and transposed up to Amin/Amaj.

The fourth bar of The B Part could instead work as “BcdB F2Bc” instead of “BcdB E2Bc”.

↳ Posted by NfldWhistler on July 10th, 2024.

Re: Le 24 Juin

Excellent X:8! Played on C whistle to work with fiddles, and only one half-hole.
Thank you NfldWhistler.

↳ Posted by John Casey on July 10th, 2024.

Re: Le 24 Juin

You’re welcome John.

The one half hole note in The A-Part, e.g., f-nat, can be replaced with a g-note instead, though, the f-nat sounds better to my ear, and is easy enough to transition from the prior e-note and to the next e-note on the whistle.

Likewise with the half hole note in The B Part, e.g., G-sharp, where it’s coming from an A-note and going back to another A-note. Tried different alternative phases for that 7th bar in The B Part, though keeping the G-sharp there is what ended up sounding better to me.

As for playing with fiddles and/or other instruments (while using a C whistle for X8), you might have to more carefully consider whether some of the alterations I made work when paired with the more “regular” setting of the tune, provided that’s what the other non-whistle/non-flute players are going by. If not, then try different alternative notes or phrases for the place(s) where it might clash until the setting works better while still being friendlier on the C whistle.

The main consideration for X8 was “friendly-ness” for the whistle, while trying to keep the general sound of the tune the same. Haven’t put as much thought into it for the above use.

↳ Posted by NfldWhistler on July 10th, 2024.
